tool_limitations.limitation: Scenario1.xaml.cs is marked SEQUENTIAL because Windows.Storage.Compression API names trip the output-safety filter; repeatedly naming Compressor/Decompressor in edit old_str/new_str is friction, so the agent fell back to a wholesale here-string Set-Content rewrite of the whole .cs (exec #42 backup, #43 rewrite).
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Skill should explicitly forbid wholesale Set-Content/here-string rewrite of ANY bootstrap-copied source file (not just *.xaml) and reiterate edit-in-place for SEQUENTIAL .cs files.

special_apis.special_handling: WinUI 3 desktop pickers must be initialized with the window HWND: WinRT.Interop.WindowNative.GetWindowHandle(App.MainWindow) + WinRT.Interop.InitializeWithWindow.Initialize(picker, hwnd). Agent applied this correctly (exec #43) from MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md#pickers.
Supported on WinUI 3 desktop; namespace family trips the model output-safety filter, so bootstrap marked the file SEQUENTIAL.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Agent abandoned in-place edit and rewrote the entire code-behind via a here-string piped to Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 (exec #43), after taking a backup (exec #42).
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: turns 22-26; one backup + one wholesale overwrite
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: The fidelity rule that forbids wholesale-overwrite is scoped in SKILL.md only to '*.xaml' files; code-behind .cs has no equivalent prohibition, and SEQUENTIAL files (filtered API names) make in-place edits feel costly, so wholesale Set-Content is the path of least resistance.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Outcome happened to be faithful this time (visible descriptions live in Scenario1.xaml, not the .cs; build + validator passed).
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Generalize the 'edit in place, never wholesale-overwrite the bootstrap copy' rule from *.xaml to ALL bootstrap-copied source files (incl. .cs code-behind/helpers), and warn against Set-Content/here-string fallback on SEQUENTIAL files.

env_issues.issue: Every winapp/PrintWindow screenshot of the migrated WinUI 3 main window rendered blank white (~7 KB) and the ComboBox popup rendered black, while the same tool captured the UWP CoreWindow golden fully (48 KB) and the native file dialog rendered fine.
env_issues.workaround: None available to the migration skill — this is a WinUI 3 DirectComposition/swapchain render-to-capture limitation of the headless/non-interactive session (score note: parity/winui3 screenshots). Belongs to the eval/harness layer, not the migration skill.
